(B) The thermal conductivity of most food materials increases with increasing moisture content; (C) In HTST pasteurization, milk is typically held at about 72°C for approximately 15 secondsDetailed Explanation:Governing concept: heat-transfer fundamentals as applied to dairy/food processing.(A) Correct — for identical terminal temperatures, counter-flow arrangement yields a higher (or equal) LMTD than parallel-flow, allowing a smaller required heat-transfer area.(B) Correct — water has much higher thermal conductivity than air/dry solids, so moist foods generally conduct heat better than dry ones.(C) Correct — the standard HTST condition is approximately 72°C for 15 s, sufficient to inactivate pathogens such as Coxiella burnetii.(D) Incorrect — the convective heat-transfer coefficient depends strongly on flow velocity (and flow regime, geometry, and fluid properties), not on thermal conductivity alone; this is reflected in correlations such as Nu = f(Re, Pr).Final Answer: (A), (B), (C).
